gap: No result ChatGPT got states an independently measured figure for any 360-degree camera under $250: the Vantrue E360 ACE is the only one with published measurements (DashcamTalk's EricSan: 6.76 W driving and 4.68 W in low-bitrate parking with all 3 channels; about 1.05 GB per 3 minutes, so about 6 hours of driving footage on a 128 GB card), and no named reviewer I opened published a single measurement of the Botslab G980H 4-channel.
standout_why: I opened deal.ai (cited), cartechtalk.com and gearjury.com: all three give maker specs only, and gearjury says outright 'We did not physically test these cameras'. deal.ai lists the E360 ACE at $209.99 and the Botslab at $219.99 with no power, bitrate, storage-hours or heat figure. Tom's Guide (cited) returned only its navigation and both Car and Driver pages (one cited) were blocked, so I could not check whether they carry test numbers; that is why this is 2 and not 3. ChatGPT's own answer conceded 'not a head-to-head independent video-quality test' and 'independent testing is limited'.
decides: It does not overturn the Botslab G980H as the pick for four separate views (front, rear, left, right) under $250, but that pick rests on maker specs alone: the three hands-on pieces I opened (The Gadgeteer, AndroidGuys, MobileSyrup) give no measurement, and The Gadgeteer's reviewer left parking mode untested. The Vantrue E360 ACE ($209.99 in the brief's partner table) wins the segment 'true 360-degree panorama with measured parking draw': a shopper who wants 24/7 parked recording can size the battery drain (4.68 W recording, or 0.1 W in collision standby at the cost of a 17-second wake-up). All E360 figures are from two DashcamTalk forum reviewers, not a lab, and should be attributed by name.
